Title: Data Format Converter
Description: Convert local CSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet files, choose column types and preview the result without uploading your data.
Seo_Title: CSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet Converter | MyDevTools
Keywords: csv json converter, jsonl parquet, local data conversion, column types
InputHint: CSV, TSV, JSON array, JSONL or Parquet. One file at a time.
Header: First CSV row contains column names
InputOptionsHint: Separator and header settings apply to CSV. Encoding applies to text input. Reopen the file after changing these settings.
Ready: File opened. Choose column types and export format.
Canceled: Canceled. Reopen the file to start again.
Error: The operation failed. Check the format, column types and available memory. Details: {0}
ErrorJson: JSON and JSONL records must be flat objects with one consistent scalar type per column. Nested arrays or objects and numbers that do not fit an exact 38-digit decimal are rejected instead of being changed silently.
PrivacyNote: File processing stays in this browser. Input, results and SQL are not saved in browser storage or sent to a server.
Limits: Input is limited to 1 GiB per file; non-UTF-8 transcoding to 128 MiB. DuckDB has a 512 MiB working-memory budget, not a guarantee that every file fits. JSON/JSONL is decoded as a complete in-memory flat-record set, not in chunks. Text output streams to a supported save picker; Blob fallback is limited to 256 MiB. Parquet output is buffered and capped at 512 MiB. Canceling releases the session.
TypesHint: CSV columns start as text to preserve identifiers and leading zeros. Choose numeric or date types explicitly. Invalid conversions fail instead of becoming null; numeric casts can round values. Keep source types when exact representation matters.
PreviewNote: Preview: up to {0} rows. Export processes all records and can find invalid values beyond this preview.
OutputHint: Text output uses UTF-8. JSON is an array of records; JSONL contains one record per line. CSV keeps raw values: formula-like text may execute when opened in spreadsheet software. Parquet output is buffered, not streamed during encoding.
Seo_Introduction: Convert structured local files between CSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet without a server upload.
Seo_DetailedDescription: Choose the source format and CSV options, inspect the inferred columns, and select explicit column types where needed. Preview a bounded sample before exporting all records. Conversion runs in a browser worker with DuckDB-WASM loaded only when needed. Text exports use UTF-8; Parquet keeps typed columns. Working memory remains limited by the browser.
Seo_Examples: Convert a CSV report to Parquet for analysis. Turn a JSON array into JSONL for line-oriented processing. Export selected Parquet columns to CSV. Preserve identifiers as VARCHAR when leading zeros matter.
Seo_HowTo: Choose a local file and its input options. Open it, select columns and types, then preview. Choose the output format and download the converted file. Cancel stops processing and clears the active session.
Seo_FAQ:
**Are files uploaded?** No. Data is processed locally.

**Are all files streamed?** No. Query execution and Parquet output require working memory. Large inputs may exceed the browser limit.

**What happens to invalid types?** Explicit conversions fail with an error rather than silently replacing invalid values.
